- A proactive attitude with a genuine willingness to learn and develop

candidates.content_text:
About the role: 
The Hills Shire Council is a growth centre with substantial built-form and land release development, and we have an exciting opportunity for a recent Development Engineer Graduate (having graduated within the last 12 months) to join our Subdivision and Development Certification Team. This role will provide the successful candidate with on-going training, ability to build on current skills sets and an opportunity to broaden your knowledge with exposure to all aspects of Subdivision and Development Certification related activities.
Working with us:
At The Hills Shire Council, we live our values of Honesty, Integrity, Loyalty, Leadership and Safety through the work that we perform for the Community. We are committed to an inclusive, diverse and supportive workplace culture where our people and customers feel respected and valued. Council also prides itself on being a Child Safe Organisation that is committed to promoting the health, safety, welfare and wellbeing of children and young people in our community.
What this role looks like:  
 - Assist under supervision to provide advice regarding Development Applications for all types of development including preparing reports, requests for information and engineering conditions of consent.
 - Assist with conducting environmental assessments for rural and urban development with regards to engineering works.
 - Assess and prepare reports for post consent approvals including but not limited to subdivision works certificates, subdivision certificates, s138/68 approvals, compliance certificates and preparation of final plans and instruments related to the registration of subdivisions.
 - Assist with inspections of public infrastructure and other post-consent matters.
What are we seeking in our new team member: 
 - Bachelors Degree in Civil, Environmental Engineering or equivalent tertiary qualifications
 - Drivers Licence (Class C) - NSW
 - White Card - General Construction Induction
Benefits of working with us:
A salary of $75K per annum (plus Superannuation) paid weekly. Opportunities for training to keep your skills up to date. An opportunity for bonus payments and to participate in wellbeing initiatives and benefits available to staff through our EBA and other programs.
Next steps:
Please review the Position Description and apply via Council’s Careers by 5pm Sunday 29 November 2026. As applications will be processed upon receipt, early submission is encouraged. Please contact Council’s HR Team at hr@thehills.nsw.gov.au if you require any assistance with submitting your application or require further information about the role or the organisation.
People with disabilities, who meet the selection criteria, are encouraged to apply. If you require any reasonable adjustments to be made or if you need any other assistance with submitting your application, please feel free to contact the HR team at hr@thehills.nsw.gov.au
Please note that recruitment and offers of employment is subject to pre-employment checks including: Psychometric Testing, Reference Checks, Identity Check, Medical checks (including Drug and Alcohol Screening), Working With Children (where applicable), and Criminal History. We assess applications on merit and suitability related to the inherent requirements of the position. Only people with the right to work in Australia may apply for this position.

candidates.content_text:
About the project John Holland is proud to be delivering the Illabo to Stockinbingal section of Inland Rail in NSW. The Illabo to Stockinbingal section is about 39km of new rail corridor located within the local government areas of Junee and Cootamundra-Gundagai. It will provide a direct route from east of Illabo, tracking north to Stockinbingal and connecting into the existing Forbes rail line.
Illabo to Stockinbingal (I2S) is a DIDO Project, accommodation is provided on the 2:1 (2 weeks on / 1 week off) roster. If you move to within an hour of Stockinbingal / Cootamundra, the Project will contribute (in line with the relocation policy) towards your relocation.
 About the Role We currently require a Site Engineer - Earthworks for the I2S project in regional NSW. Your role will be pivotal in supporting the broader construction teams with planning works, coordinating subcontractors, ensuring quality, OHS and environment deliverables are met, and construction progress reporting.
 What you will do - Plan and coordinate construction activities, including short and medium-term programming, to support safe, efficient and timely project delivery.
 - Provide technical engineering support on site, resolving construction and design issues and identifying practical solutions that improve constructability.
 - Ensure works comply with technical specifications, legislation, approvals, standards and project safety, quality and environmental requirements.
 - Support the commercial management of the project, including cost control, estimating, budget management and verification of subcontractor claims and variations.
 - Monitor and report on project performance, including risks, quality, defects and non-conformances, while maintaining accurate project documentation and drawing controls.
 What we are looking for - Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, with postgraduate qualifications viewed favourably.
 - Experience delivering civil construction projects in Australia, ideally across major infrastructure works.
 - Previous experience with a Tier 1 or Tier 2 contractor is highly regarded.
 - Strong understanding of civil construction and project delivery in a site-based engineering environment.
 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant project systems, with Aconex experience considered an advantage
 What we offer 
 • Competitive salary and benefits, including salary continuance and salary sacrifice options
 • Flexible work arrangements and generous leave, including 18 weeks paid parental leave
 • Career development through technical, leadership and emerging talent programs
 • Opportunities to work on some of Australia's most iconic projects
 • A diverse and inclusive culture where everyone feels they belong
 • Wellbeing support and benefits designed to help you thrive
 At John Holland, our purpose is simple: we transform lives with everything we do.
 We know infrastructure is about people - our customers, our employees and the communities we work in every day. That's what sets us apart: deep expertise, proven capability and a genuine commitment to creating better outcomes for people along the way.
 With expertise spanning engineering, construction and operations, we're delivering the projects and services that keep communities moving. From rail, roads and bridges to hospitals and stadiums, we've helped shape Australia through iconic projects. You'll even see us operating buses, trains and trams.
 Be part of a team that's up for the challenge of transforming lives.
 John Holland does not accept any speculative or unsolicited CV's from agencies that have been sent to our internal recruitment team or hiring managers.

bullets: Help shape Bielby's growth across NSW

candidates.content_text:
Bielby is experiencing a period of sustained growth, supported by a strong pipeline of major infrastructure opportunities and continued expansion into new regions. Building on over 40 years of successful major project delivery, we are seeking experienced Civil Engineers at all levels to join our team in NSW and be part of the first major infrastructure project win in NSW.
Bielby has been awarded the Kempsey-Armidale Road Restoration Project (K2A) by Armidale Regional Council, marking our first major award since establishing a permanent NSW presence in early 2026. It also represents our largest infrastructure restoration and recovery contract to date, a key pillar of Bielby’s growth and diversification strategy.
The project will restore 43 kilometres of Kempsey-Armidale Road and a five-kilometre section of Lower Creek Road following damage caused by the 2019 bushfires and subsequent flood events in 2020 and 2022. Once complete, the works will help reconnect communities, support regional industries and improve the resilience of an important transport corridor linking Armidale with the NSW coast.
You will be part of a $400M major regional infrastructure project that will restore and strengthen critical transport links across regional New South Wales. More importantly, it is an opportunity to play a key role in Bielby's strategic expansion within NSW.
What You'll Do
- Coordinate and/or support site activities, subcontractors, suppliers and resources to safely deliver against project requirements.
- Monitor quantities, productivity and costs and contribute to forecasting, reporting and the management of variations.
- Build strong relationships across project teams, clients, subcontractors and other stakeholders.
- Contribute to a safe, inclusive and high-performing team environment.
- For our more experienced engineers, provide guidance and support to developing engineers and contribute to broader project planning and decision-making.
What You'll Bring
- A Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
- Experience in civil construction or infrastructure appropriate to your level.
- Practical problem-solving skills and sound engineering judgement.
- The ability to communicate clearly and build effective working relationships.
- A collaborative approach and willingness to contribute across different stages of the project lifecycle.
- For senior opportunities, the ability to lead and develop others, set clear expectations and create a collaborative, accountable team environment.
- A willingness to do a DIDO roster
Why Bielby?
The Bielby Way – Where People Matter
At Bielby, you'll get the opportunity to work on complex, meaningful infrastructure while being part of a business where your contribution is visible, your voice is valued and you're trusted to get on with the job.
We're proudly Australian owned and operated, with more than 40 years of experience and a strong reputation for delivering major civil infrastructure. With a strong pipeline and an expanding geographic footprint, we're creating new opportunities for our people and their careers.
What you can expect:
- Real responsibility and a genuine voice – we empower capable people to make decisions, solve problems and take ownership.
- Career growth through experience – build your technical, commercial and leadership capability through hands-on experience, mentoring, internal mobility and development opportunities.
- Complex projects that make an impact – contribute to infrastructure that connects communities and leaves a lasting legacy.
- A highly engaged culture – our latest employee engagement score is 17% above the industry average.
- People genuinely matter – safety, wellbeing, respect, honesty and collaboration are central to how we work.
- Competitive rewards and benefits – including competitive remuneration, project uplifts for eligible regional/FIFO/DIDO assignments, paid parental leave, wellbeing support and employee benefits.
- A workplace that values different perspectives – we're committed to belonging and inclusion and are a corporate member of NAWIC, providing all employees access to networking, mentoring and professional development opportunities.
As Bielby grows, you grow with us.
Interested? We'd like to hear from you.
Successful applicants will be required to undergo a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol checks.
Applicants must have eligibility to work in Australia.

About Kilcomer Group
Kilcomer Group is a privately owned construction and labour hire business based in Camden/Narellan. We work as a specialist subcontractor to tier 1 and tier 2 head contractors including Acciona, CPB,Seymour Whyte and McConnell Dowell, delivering civil, structural and specialist works on bridges, dams, water infrastructure and major projects across NSW, ACT, QLD and SA. We're a hands-on team that moves fast, and we're growing.
The role

Your degree gave you the theory. Now it's time to experience the real thing.
Kickstart your career with real-world construction experience!  
Are you a recent engineering graduate looking to build practical experience, develop your technical knowledge and gain exposure to a diverse range of construction projects?
At Waterproofing Integrity, we're offering an exciting opportunity to join our Compliance Inspection team, working across live construction sites and engaging with a broad range of builders, contractors and industry professionals, including leading Tier 1 and Tier 2 builders.
This isn't your typical graduate role. You'll be out on site, learning from experienced industry professionals, understanding how buildings come together and developing skills that will support your long-term engineering career.
What you'll be doing  
- Conducting compliance inspections and testing of waterproofing membrane installations on active construction sites.
- Gaining exposure to diverse construction projects, working with builders, contractors and consultants, including Tier 1 and Tier 2 construction companies.
- Learning how to assess, measure, quantify and document waterproofing installations against project specifications and relevant standards.
- Preparing professional inspection reports, recording findings and communicating outcomes.
- Developing an understanding of construction methodologies, building design and the critical role waterproofing plays in structural durability and performance.
- Building confidence in communicating with site supervisors, project managers, engineers and other stakeholders.
What you'll gain  
Real construction experience: Get hands-on exposure to a variety of live projects and see how engineering principles translate into practical construction outcomes.
Training and development: Receive structured on-the-job training, technical guidance and ongoing support from experienced professionals.
Professional skills: Strengthen your communication, technical reporting, problem-solving and stakeholder engagement capabilities.
Industry exposure: Build experience across different construction environments, including projects delivered by leading Tier 1 and Tier 2 builders, as well as a broad range of other construction developments.
What we're looking for  
We're looking for graduates who are motivated, curious and ready to learn.
Exceptional communication skills are paramount to success in this role. You'll be representing Waterproofing Integrity on construction sites, engaging with a range of stakeholders and communicating technical findings clearly, confidently and professionally.
To be considered, you'll need:
- A completed engineering degree or relevant tertiary qualification.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the confidence to engage professionally with clients, builders and site personnel.
- A genuine willingness to learn and develop new technical capabilities.
- Strong attention to detail and an organised approach to documentation and reporting.
- A current, valid Australian driver's licence.
- Flexibility and availability to travel to different project sites.
- A positive attitude, initiative and a commitment to delivering quality outcomes.
- White Card
An understanding of the construction industry, building practices or waterproofing systems will be highly regarded, but is not essential. We value attitude, communication skills and a willingness to learn, and we'll provide the training and support needed to develop your technical knowledge.
Why Waterproofing Integrity?  
Waterproofing is one of the most critical components of building performance, yet it's an area many engineering graduates have had limited exposure to during their studies.
At Waterproofing Integrity, you'll gain an understanding of how waterproofing systems are designed, installed, tested and assessed — and why getting it right matters.
You'll also gain exposure to the broader construction industry, working with a variety of project teams and developing an understanding of compliance, technical standards and construction practices across different building environments.
This opportunity will help bridge the gap between university and industry, giving you practical experience, technical knowledge and professional confidence as you begin your career.
Our Recruitment Process  
We're looking for graduates who can demonstrate more than just academic achievement. Communication, attitude and a genuine interest in developing a career in the construction industry are important to us.
Further details will be provided to candidates as they progress through the recruitment process.
Ready to put your degree into practice?  
If you're a motivated engineering graduate with excellent communication skills, a positive attitude and a genuine desire to learn, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply now with your CV and a short introduction telling us why you're interested in developing your career in construction compliance and inspection.
Applications are open for our January 2027 intake and close on Friday 4th December 4.00pm

At BildGroup, we’re passionate about helping you make the most of your journey with us. Our focus is giving you the tools and support you need to be your best, along with the recognition and rewards for jobs well done.
- Your development: From online learning and hands-on training to mentorship and lunch and learns, we invest in helping you grow.

Our Urban division is delivering a subdivision project in Echuca, and we need a Project or Site Engineer on the ground to help deliver it. You will work on site alongside the project team, supervisors and subcontractors, looking after the engineering, quality and documentation that keep the job on program and to specification.
BildGroup already has an established presence in Echuca. This role suits an engineer who lives in or around Echuca-Moama, or an experienced engineer ready to relocate to the region.

Australian-owned for more than 45 years, BildGroup measures success not by what we build, but by how our people grow and the places we work in change for the better.  As a national multidisciplinary civil infrastructure contractor, we connect and shape the communities we live in, from metropolitan growth corridors to remote and regional communities.

Civil Design Engineer
 Location: Brisbane, QLD
 The Opportunity
 We are seeking an experienced Civil Design Engineer to join an established multidisciplinary engineering consultancy in Brisbane, working across a diverse range of road and transport infrastructure projects throughout Queensland.
 This is an excellent opportunity for a technically capable engineer with 5+ years of experience in civil design, particularly across DTMR road and highway projects. You will play an important role in the design and delivery of transport infrastructure projects, contributing to engineering solutions across various stages of the project lifecycle.
 Working closely with experienced engineers, designers and project managers, you will have the opportunity to take ownership of design deliverables, collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and contribute to the successful delivery of road and highway infrastructure projects.
 About the Company
 Our client is an established multidisciplinary engineering consultancy providing civil engineering, infrastructure design and project delivery services across Queensland.
 With a strong presence in the Queensland market, the business works across a diverse portfolio of infrastructure projects, offering engineers the opportunity to develop their technical capabilities and contribute to significant transport infrastructure developments.
 Key Responsibilities
 - Undertake civil engineering design for road, highway and transport infrastructure projects.
 - Prepare concept and detailed designs for road alignments, intersections, interchanges and associated civil infrastructure.
 - Contribute to the design and delivery of DTMR and local government road infrastructure projects.
 - Prepare and review engineering drawings, design calculations, technical reports and specifications.
 - Utilise civil design software including 12d Model and AutoCAD to develop engineering designs.
 - Ensure designs comply with relevant DTMR standards, Austroads guidelines and Australian Standards.
 - Coordinate design activities and technical deliverables across multidisciplinary engineering teams.
 - Liaise with clients, government authorities, consultants and other project stakeholders.
 - Identify and resolve technical design challenges throughout the project lifecycle.
 - Contribute to projects from initial concept development through to detailed design and construction support.
 About You
 To be successful in this role, you will have:
 - A minimum of 5 years' experience in civil engineering design within an engineering consultancy environment.
 - A degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
 - Demonstrated experience in road and highway design, ideally across DTMR projects.
 - Strong technical knowledge of road geometry, alignments, intersections and associated civil infrastructure.
 - Experience using 12d Model, AutoCAD or other relevant civil design software.
 - A sound understanding of DTMR design requirements, Austroads guidelines and relevant Australian Standards.
 - Experience contributing to transport infrastructure projects from concept through to detailed design.
 - Strong technical design capabilities and the ability to prepare and review engineering documentation.
 - Experience working collaboratively with multidisciplinary engineering teams.
 - Strong communication, problem-solving and project coordination skills.
 - The ability to manage competing priorities and take ownership of design deliverables.
 - A proactive approach to engineering challenges and a desire to further develop your technical expertise.
 Previous experience delivering Queensland DTMR road and highway projects will be highly regarded.
 RPEQ registration, or progress towards obtaining registration, will also be advantageous.
 Apply Now
 If you are an experienced Civil Design Engineer looking to further develop your career within the transport infrastructure sector and gain exposure to a diverse range of road and highway projects, we would like to hear from you.
 Please contact Ronan Brady on 0466 697 586 or email your CV to ronan.brady@cgcrecruitment.com.

Civil Engineer | Dubbo, NSW
Build your career. Shape your future. Make a difference in regional NSW.
Are you a Civil Engineer looking for more than just your next project? Here's an opportunity to join an established engineering consultancy, play an important role in the continued growth of our Dubbo office and help shape the future of the local team.
We're looking for a capable, motivated mid-level Civil Engineer who is ready to take the next step in their career. You'll have the opportunity to broaden your technical experience, take ownership of projects and work towards greater responsibility, with genuine opportunities for career progression as the team grows. 
Why Dubbo? A great place to build your career and your life.
Dubbo offers the best of both worlds: the professional opportunities of a regional engineering centre with the lifestyle benefits that come from living outside a major city.
With a strong sense of community, affordable living, excellent schools, outdoor recreation and a relaxed pace of life, Dubbo is an attractive place to put down roots. Enjoy easy access to parks, the Macquarie River, cafes, restaurants and the surrounding Central West region, without the long commutes and congestion of metropolitan living.
For someone looking to establish themselves professionally while enjoying a better lifestyle, Dubbo is well worth considering.
About the Role
Working as part of our Civil Engineering team, you'll contribute to a diverse range of civil infrastructure and development projects across regional NSW.
This is a hands-on consulting engineering role where you'll combine technical design capability with project delivery and client engagement.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Preparing civil engineering designs, calculations, technical reports and specifications.
- Developing concept and detailed design drawings for a range of infrastructure projects.
- Working across urban development, subdivision and regional civil infrastructure projects.
- Coordinating design delivery and contributing to project management activities.
- Liaising with clients, local councils, contractors and other project stakeholders.
- Undertaking site inspections and providing engineering advice.
- Supporting and contributing to the development of the local engineering team.
You'll have the opportunity to take ownership of your work, develop client relationships and gradually expand your project and leadership responsibilities.
What we’re looking for
We're interested in someone with solid consulting engineering experience who is technically capable, takes pride in their work and wants to be part of something they're helping to build.
You'll ideally bring:
- A Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering.
- Around 3+ years' experience in civil engineering consultancy.
- Experience delivering civil design and documentation for infrastructure or land development projects.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD and 12d Model.
- An understanding of relevant civil engineering standards, codes and design principles.
- Strong communication skills and the confidence to engage with clients and stakeholders.
- The ability to manage competing priorities and take responsibility for project deliverables.
Experience with the following would be advantageous:
- Stormwater and drainage design, including DRAINS and MUSIC.
- Regional infrastructure and subdivision projects.
- Project coordination and client management.
Importantly, we're looking for someone with ambition. You don't need to have all the answers today, but you should be keen to develop your technical capability, take on more responsibility and grow into a key member of the team.
We are also open to considering Senior Civil Engineers with suitable consulting experience who are seeking their next opportunity, with the scope of the role able to be tailored accordingly.
The Team and Environment
At Amey, we bring together engineering expertise and local knowledge to deliver practical outcomes for the communities in which we work.
Our Dubbo office is an important part of our regional presence, and this appointment is about investing in its future.
You'll work alongside experienced engineering professionals, with access to broader technical expertise and support across our Australian business and wider Amey network.
We're looking for someone who wants to contribute, not simply turn up and complete allocated design tasks. Someone who enjoys being involved in projects, building relationships and helping develop the capability of the local team.
Why Join Us?
- Career progression: Genuine opportunities to develop towards Senior Engineer and beyond as your capability and experience grow.
- Professional development: Work alongside experienced engineers and access broader technical expertise across the business.
- Variety of projects: Gain exposure to diverse civil infrastructure and regional development projects.
- Opportunity to make an impact: Play an important role in the future growth of our Dubbo office.
- Lifestyle: Enjoy the affordability, community and lifestyle benefits of regional NSW.
- Established business: Be part of Amey, an international engineering and infrastructure organisation with a growing Australian presence.
- Flexible working arrangements available.
- Birthday leave day to celebrate you.
- Health & Wellness benefit to the value of $250.
- Employee Assistance Program.
- Regular Lunch & learn sessions.
- Milestone Recognition

Joining Arup
Arup's purpose, shared values and collaborative approach have set us apart for 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world.
Join our NSW/ACT Roads team and become part of an extraordinary collective where diverse perspectives, shared ambition and collaboration drive remarkable outcomes. You will contribute to road infrastructure projects that strengthen communities, improve transport outcomes and support more sustainable places. The Opportunity
As a Roads Engineer, you will support the delivery and communication of road infrastructure designs across a variety of highways and road projects whilst developing your skills in a supportive environment under the guide of a mentor. Working with government agencies, construction contractors and private developers, you will undertake civil engineering design, prepare technical documentation and contribute to reports, cost estimates, tender submissions, project programmes and meetings. improvement

Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup.

candidates.content_text:
Council is seeking an experienced, passionate and customer-focused Transport Engineer to support sustainable and active transport throughout our Local Government Area.
North Sydney Council administers the North Sydney local government area on Sydney’s picturesque lower North Shore. Our 400 employees look after 77,000 residents spread across 10 square kilometres of land on the foreshores of Sydney Harbour providing spectacular harbour views, beautiful parklands, and a bustling CBD. Our aim is to ensure North Sydney remains a welcoming, well-designed, safe and beautiful environment for residents, workers and visitors.
The role 
As a Transport Engineer, you’ll play an important role in shaping how people move around North Sydney, supporting the delivery of Council’s Integrated Transport Strategy and leading initiatives that promote safer, more accessible and sustainable transport options.
Working within the Transport team, you’ll investigate and develop practical solutions to improve road safety, access, kerbside management, and walking and cycling infrastructure. You’ll undertake technical assessments, site investigations and data analysis, prepare reports and recommendations, and contribute to the planning and implementation of active and sustainable transport projects.
You’ll also work closely with the community, internal teams, government agencies and industry stakeholders, providing technical advice, assessing development applications and supporting projects that enhance connectivity, accessibility and the overall experience of moving around North Sydney.
The person 
We're looking for a motivated and solutions-focused Transport Engineer who brings sound technical knowledge of transport planning and engineering principles, guidelines, standards and contemporary practices.
You have a keen interest in sustainable and active transport and enjoy applying your technical expertise to develop practical solutions to complex transport challenges. 
You’re a confident communicator who enjoys building collaborative relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders, while maintaining a strong customer focus and commitment to achieving positive outcomes for the community.
Why work at NSC? 
We're committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and positive workplace. Our teams are reflective of the communities in which we operate, and we value the unique contribution each member makes to the North Sydney Council. The work we do makes a real difference to the lives of our residents and contributes to their economic and social wellbeing.
North Sydney Council as an employer offers excellent employee benefits such as:
- Easy accessibility to work with spectacular harbour view work locations
- Access to Fitness Passport 
- Excellent work-life balance with a 35-hour working week for indoor employees or fortnightly RDO’s for outdoor employees
- Flexible working hours with access to flexi-time for indoor employees
- Freedom to direct contributions to any compliant superannuation fund
- A holistic health and well-being program offering exercise classes, flu vaccinations, skin checks, and a touch football team
- Health and Well-being programs for all employees such as Yoga, Pilates, Kick Boxing
- Access to employee recognition and reward program
- Weekly fruit baskets
- Free access to counselling sessions through our Employee Assistance Program
- Free financial advice by a certified Financial Planner
- Monetary transport allowance
- Invitations to local government events, training and planning sessions
- Access to corporate social events at picturesque harbour locations
- Close locale to transport options including train, bus, metro and bike ways 
Salary Range: $108,378 to $129,412 per annum + 3.5% Civil Liability allowance + $1,000 pa Transport allowance + 12% superannuation  
35 hours per week with access to flex time 
How to apply
Applicants are required to submit a resume and provide a statement of what makes you the most suitable candidate for the role. 
Candidates who regularly use a bicycle or other micromobility device for transport, and have completed the NSW Training course Designing for Pedestrians and Bicycle Riders, or an equivalent course, will be highly regarded.

North Sydney Council is committed to the principles of Equal Employment Opportunity in order to provide a working environment that embraces and values diversity and inclusion. North Sydney Council also adheres to the principles of a child safe organisation and is committed to the care and protection of all children and young people. We strongly encourage candidates from wide-ranging backgrounds, identities and experiences to apply.

Permanent
Full-time (average of 38 hours per week)
The City of Rockingham is an award winning local government located 40km south of the Perth CBD and is known as the place where the coast comes to life.  One of the fastest growing local governments in the south metropolitan area, we are responsible for the provision and delivery of high quality services, facilities and events that meet or exceed community expectations.  Providing a safe and healthy workplace for our employees is important to us and we are committed to employing team members who share the City’s Values of Recognition, Ethics, Service, Professional Development, Empowerment, Communication and Teamwork – RESPECT. These Values are incorporated into all aspects of employment at the City.
We are seeking an experienced and motivated Development Engineer to provide expert engineering advice and coordinate the assessment of land development proposals, ensuring high-quality infrastructure outcomes that support sustainable urban growth.
About the role
As a Development Engineer, you will coordinate and assess the civil engineering aspects of development, including Urban Water Management Plans, Structure Plans, Development Applications and Subdivision Applications. This role requires significant technical expertise in civil infrastructure, drainage, traffic safety and development processes, together with the ability to provide specialist advice and undertake complex engineering analysis.
The position is responsible for assessing and approving engineering designs for civil infrastructure within developments, coordinating inspections of subdivision works to be taken over by the City, and ensuring infrastructure is delivered to the required standards. You will also contribute to the development and implementation of engineering policies, guidelines and standards relating to civil infrastructure and traffic safety pertaining to land development, while providing technical input into complex reports and recommendations.
To be successful in this role, you will bring extensive experience in land development processes together with a demonstrated ability to assess and manage complex development proposals, subdivision applications and civil infrastructure projects. You will possess a strong understanding of relevant Western Australia legislation, policies, standards and approval processes, and a proven track record of providing high-level technical advice, coordinating stakeholder engagement, experience of leading a team and delivering sound engineering outcomes. This position is suited to an experienced engineering professional who is confident navigating complex development matters and delivering practical, risk-based solutions in a dynamic development environment.
Previous Australian local government experience is desirable. 
To be considered for this role, you must address the following selection criteria as part of your online application:
- Briefly describe your experience managing land subdivision and development projects, including greenfield subdivisions and/or urban infill developments. Please include your involvement in planning approvals, subdivision processes and compliance with relevant Western Australia statutory requirements.
- Briefly describe a complex engineering or development project where you analysed technical data and assessed design elements relating to road and drainage infrastructure.
- Provide a brief overview of your experience in the planning, design, construction and delivery of civil engineering related works, including your experience managing contractors, consultants and service providers.
- Briefly describe your experience in the modelling and implementation of urban water management concepts.
- Provide a brief example that demonstrates your written and verbal communication skills, including your experience of communicating technical information to stakeholders and preparing technical reports.
- Briefly describe your experience leading, supervising or developing staff within an engineering environment.
- Outline your experience of software packages such as 3D Civil.
- Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering or acquisition of skills and extensive relevant experience in the field of engineering development
Please refer to other “Essential Requirements” of the Job, as outlined in the position description which is included in the information package (available from the City of Rockingham Job Vacancies page).
What we offer
This position offers a gross annual salary of $120,603 - $128,590 per annum and:
- 12% superannuation with the option to co-contribute up to a further 5%
- Flexible working arrangements, including rostered days off and two additional paid days of absence per year
- A variety of health and wellbeing programs including a physical health reimbursement subsidy payment of up to $200 per annum, free flu vaccinations, free skin cancer checks, mental health programs and Employee Assistance Provider (EAP) services
- Training and development opportunities including paid study leave and study fees
- Salary packaging opportunities for motor vehicles, etc.
Applications are open until 4pm on 4 December 2026; or until a suitable pool of applicants has been received.
Applications will be reviewed as they are received, and interviews may commence prior to the closing date. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
The City reserves the right to close applications early, should it consider a suitable pool of candidates have been received.  This means the position may close without notice. If you are interested in the position, we highly recommend that you apply as soon as possible.
This process may be used to fill future similar permanent or fixed-term positions that may become available in the City during the next 12 months.
If you identify as a person with disability and require adjustments throughout the recruitment and selection process please contact the Recruitment Team via email at jobs@rockingham.wa.gov.au or phone 08 9528 0333. We’re happy to discuss options to assist you e.g. we can provide alternate formats for application forms, or alternate methods of applying.

candidates.content_text:
- $130,264 base + 16.5% Super + a fortnightly Rostered Day Off
- Permanent full time

About Ausgrid – we’re wired for good
 We’re the largest distributor of electricity on Australia’s east coast, which means over two million homes and businesses rely on our good work. We’re here at the heart of the energy transition, and we’re driven by a powerful purpose to make electricity accessible for all.
It’s an exciting new chapter for our company with each day bringing a renewed energy to how we deliver, store and use electricity. As we continue to grow, we’re in search of exceptional talent to help us achieve our goals.
Everyone’s job is important here. Our customers come from all walks of life, and so do we. We’re committed to fostering a diverse, respectful, and inclusive workplace, and encourage applications from all backgrounds.
See yourself working here
Reporting to the Connection Delivery Manager – Central Region, the ANS Engineering Officer is responsible for managing, coordinating and facilitating a broad range of customer-requested works associated with the Ausgrid network. The role supports the safe, efficient and timely delivery of customer connections, network access activities and network-related safety services, ensuring customer requirements are appropriately assessed and progressed in accordance with relevant Ausgrid processes, standards and operational requirements.
The ANS Engineering Officer acts as a key point of coordination between customers, contractors, Accredited Service Providers, industry partners and internal Ausgrid teams. This involves understanding customer requirements, identifying the appropriate pathway for delivery, coordinating the necessary network activities and documentation, and supporting the resolution of technical, operational and access-related issues as they arise.
A strong focus of the role is maintaining effective stakeholder relationships and providing clear, practical guidance throughout the delivery process. By coordinating competing requirements, maintaining accurate records and proactively progressing customer requests, the ANS Engineering Officer contributes to positive customer outcomes while ensuring safety, network integrity and compliance remain central to the delivery of all works.
What you bring to the role
Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Preparation, coordination and submission of Network Access Requests to support planned customer works.
- Assessment of customer-requested works, including reviewing requirements, determining the appropriate scope of work and preparing accurate quotations.
- Preparation and provision of Safety Advice for customers and third parties undertaking work in the vicinity of Ausgrid assets, supporting safe work practices and appropriate controls.

Company description:
 About DT Infrastructure
 DT Infrastructure is a trusted provider of engineering and construction solutions that unlock opportunities for our clients, communities and people. Specialising in Defence, transport and infrastructure, we offer a unique synergy of local expertise in complex projects and the global perspective of our multinational parent company, Gamuda Berhad. Through engineering innovation, collaborative contracting and leading sustainability practices we're unlocking opportunities for a better tomorrow.
Job description:
 About the role
 DT Infrastructure is seeking an experienced Project Engineer to join our growing South Australian Rail Team, who will provide engineering, technical, quality support and other duties as delegated by the Project Manager and Operations Manager.
 This role is a full-time position where you will be working on a 10:4 DIDO roster.
 Key responsibilities include:
 - Coordinate and support the delivery of signalling construction activities, ensuring works are completed safely, on schedule, to budget and in compliance with project, client and rail industry requirements.
 - Review signalling design documentation, drawings, specifications, circuit books and construction work packs to ensure construction readiness, constructability and technical compliance.
 - Manage technical interfaces between signalling, track, civil, electrical, communications and commissioning teams, resolving technical queries and supporting design changes throughout project delivery.
 - Monitor construction progress, quality and compliance, including the preparation and administration of ITPs, inspection records, construction certification, as-built documentation, defects and non-conformance management.
 - Support project planning, procurement and resource coordination, identifying and escalating programme risks, access constraints, material shortages and other issues that may impact delivery outcomes.
 - Foster strong relationships with clients, subcontractors and project stakeholders while promoting a culture of safety, continuous improvement, accountability and engineering excellence across the project team.
 Experience and capabilities
 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering and eligibility for membership with Engineers Australia, with at least 3 years' experience in construction, infrastructure or engineering project delivery environments.
 - Demonstrated experience in project planning, programming and site engineering, with the ability to manage competing priorities, schedules and project deliverables effectively.
 - Strong technical and commercial acumen, including the ability to interpret engineering documentation, contractual requirements, legislation, standards and organisational procedures.
 - Proven stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with clients, subcontractors, suppliers and internal teams to achieve successful project outcomes.
 - Well-developed analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with experience researching complex issues, assessing risks and implementing practical, value-driven solutions.
 - Highly motivated and self-driven professional with excellent communication, negotiation and organisational skills, capable of working autonomously while contributing to a high-performing team culture.
 Why work for DTI
 - Competitive pay that reflects your contribution: We reward performance and impact, with our remuneration benchmarked to market. 
 - Purpose-driven careers in infrastructure: As we grow our presence in the renewable energy sector, DTI is also continuing to cement its position as a delivery partner of choice across rail, roads and Defence infrastructure projects. Our teams benefit from the variety of opportunities, applying their skills and experience across multiple sectors. 
 - Fostering your development: We've developed a culture where continuous learning is front and centre of everything we do. Fostering the growth and development of our people is key to our success and ensuring that we are preparing the next generation of leaders is a core focus for our business. 
 - Parental leave designed for the reality of family life: Our industry leading parental leave policies are centred on flexibility to support modern family life, because at DTI, little families are a part of our one big family. 
 - Flexibility that works for you and for us: We acknowledge that everyone's needs are different in striking the right work-life integration. Whether it's hybrid working, adjusted hours, job sharing or balancing family commitments, we'll work together to make it work. 
DT Infrastructure is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace that champions opportunity and respect. Our focus on inclusivity is active and ongoing. Women, people of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Island descent and former members of the Australian Defence Force are encouraged to apply.
 Visit www.DTInfrastructure.com.au to explore how DTI can support your career progression, unlock personal advantages and apply for our opportunities.
 How to apply
 If you are looking to make a meaningful impact and join our team, we would love to hear from you. Please submit your updated CV online to be considered for this role. 
If you have any questions or issues submitting your application, please reach out to careers@dtinfrastructure.com.au.

Join Arup

The Opportunity
As a Pavement Engineer, you will develop practical, safe, sustainable and technically robust pavement solutions. Working under limited supervision, you will take ownership of defined tasks and work packages while continuing to build your technical, project management and client engagement capability.

·   A minimum of five years’ experience in pavement design and construction, including experience across medium to large-scale infrastructure projects.

candidates.content_text:
About Endeavour Engineering
Endeavour Engineering is a remedial engineering consultancy specialising in building diagnostic inspections and remedial waterproofing design. Our work focuses on assessing the condition of existing buildings, identifying the cause of defects, and developing practical repair solutions that address water ingress and durability issues and protect structural performance.
A key part of our practice involves the preparation of technical reports for building defect matters, including matters that may proceed to dispute resolution or litigation. We regularly work alongside legal advisers, strata managers, property owners, and Owners Corporations. Our role is to provide clear, evidence-based engineering advice to support informed decision-making and long-term asset protection.
The Role
We are excited to offer an outstanding opportunity to join our growing organisation as a Graduate Remedial Engineer on a full-time basis. Based in our Western Sydney, NSW office, you will also have the chance to work on diverse and impactful projects across Sydney, the Illawarra, the Central Coast, and regional NSW.
This position is suited to a recent engineering graduate who is seeking a technically rigorous environment that encourages independent thinking and professional judgement. You will be provided with the tools, systems, and exposure necessary to develop practical remedial engineering skills through site inspections, defect investigations, reporting, and remedial design documentation, while working within a team of experienced engineers.
Key Responsibilities
Your day will be busy and varied, including:
- The role involves assisting experienced engineers with site inspections of residential, commercial, and industrial buildings. You will attend sites to observe building defects, take measurements, record photographic evidence, and assist with documenting site conditions. Some inspections may occur outside metropolitan Sydney.
- You will assist in the preparation of technical reports that describe observed defects, likely causes, and proposed remedial options. This includes contributing to reports used for general advisory purposes and, where required, for dispute or litigation matters.
- You will support the preparation of remedial design documentation by providing mark-ups, sketches, and technical input, and by working closely with our in-house drafting team to develop regulated design drawings.
- You will assist with project coordination tasks, including organising site access, liaising with contractors and specialist consultants, and maintaining clear records of inspections and correspondence.
- Under supervision, you will contribute to quality assurance processes by reviewing drawings and reports for completeness, clarity, and consistency with Endeavour Engineering standards.
Qualifications & Experience
- You must hold a Bachelor's degree in Engineering with a civil or structural focus. Prior experience in remedial or forensic engineering is not essential but will be viewed favourably.
- Candidates must hold a completed Bachelor's degree in Engineering
- You shall have a basic understanding of structural behaviour and an interest in building defects, waterproofing, and remedial construction. Familiarity with the Building Code of Australia and Australian Standards is desirable and will be developed further in the role.
- You must have strong written communication skills and the ability to present technical information clearly and logically. You must be able to work both independently and as part of a small technical team.
Other Requirements:
- Possession of a current driver's licence and access to a car
- Fluency in English and eligibility to work in Australia.
- Candidates must have current Australian work authorisation at the time of application.
- Candidates must hold Australian citizenship or permanent residency status.
What We Offer
- We offer a competitive graduate salary aligned with experience and qualifications. You will receive direct mentoring from senior engineers with extensive experience in remedial engineering and building defect matters.
- The role provides structured on-the-job learning, exposure to real projects, and a clear pathway for professional development within a supportive small business environment. You will gain practical experience across inspections, reporting, and remedial design, with ongoing training provided internally and externally as appropriate.
Recruitment agencies and recruiters: Please do not contact us regarding this position. We welcome applications directly from candidates.
